newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico army raids hotel seeking drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Mexico army raids hotel seeking drug lord.

text.p: Mexican soldiers raided a posh hotel in this central Mexican city late on Thursday, reportedly in search of a top drug lord.
Some 50 troops stormed the Carlton hotel in downtown Guadalajara and searched every floor, Salvador Gonzalez Puga, head of hotel security, told Reuters.
Mexico City radio station Radio Red reported the troops were looking for Amado Carrillo Fuentes, Mexico's most wanted drug kingpin and head of the powerful Juarez drug cartel.
Gonzalez Puga contradicted a report that five people had been arrested.
"It was a thourough revision of the whole hotel. There were at least 50 soldiers. No one was arrested," Gonzalez Puga said.
State-owned news agency Notimex quoted hotel manager Jose Luis Rodriguez, however, as saying the army had arrested five unidentified people.
Mexican police and the army were unavailable for comment on the reports.
Carrillo Fuentes hit the headlines recently when Mexico arrested its top anti-drug official, an army general, on charges he was working for Carrillo Fuentes.
Mexico has been eager to defend its anti-drugs credentials amid intense scrutiny from the United States, which recently certified that Mexico was an ally in the drugs war despite heavy opposition.

However, a U.S. House of Representatives committee voted on Thursday to overturn President Bill Clinton's finding that Mexico is fully cooperating in the anti-drug war but to waive imposition of sanctions against the Mexican government.
Over administration objections, the International Relations Committee voted 27-5 to send the measure to the full House for action. Similar legislation has been introduced in the U.S. Senate.
